status: measured and off: no published declaration reads this file. metadata/sources.json (treasury_auctions, scheduled_availability) stays the declaration every published record is scored under, because the final-test pre-registration freezes it by its bytes. Eleonora ruled on 10 October 2026 (relayed by the orchestrating session on #541) that a settlement is dated from the auction announcement; turning it on in the published declaration is a later pull request, made once she has merged the amendment to docs/decisions/information-set.md that this pull request drafts.

columns.treasury_settlement: every auction settling on the day
columns.treasury_settlement_bills: the auctions whose security_type is a declared bill type (contract.TREASURY_BILL_SECURITY_TYPES)
columns.treasury_settlement_coupons: the auctions whose security_type is a declared coupon type (contract.TREASURY_COUPON_SECURITY_TYPES)

rule: An auction's settlement date (issue_date) and offering amount (offering_amt) are public from its announcement: 12:00 New York time on its announcemt_date. For the forecast made h panel days before a settlement day d, at the declared decision time on that panel day, a settlement column for d is the sum, in USD billions, of the offering amounts of the auctions settling on d that had been announced by 12:00 on that day. An auction not yet announced is not in the sum. The announcement fixes the offering, so an auction that has not been held, or whose result is not on file, is in the sum from its announcement. At h = 1 this is the published panel's column on every panel day, because every auction settling inside the panel was announced before it was held (the tracked snapshot's announcemt_date never follows auction_date), and was held at least one panel day before it settled (sources.json, treasury_auctions, scheduled_availability evidence).
missing: A record with no announcemt_date, or one dated after its auction or after its settlement, is refused (ValueError): it would date the settlement from nothing or from after it happened. A settlement day with no auction on file reads 0.0 inside the snapshot's coverage, as the published panel does (data.build_daily_panel rule 8), and a hole outside it. treasury_settlement_soma, an auction result outside the aggregate, is not dated by this declaration and is a hole under it.
evidence: The tracked snapshot tests/fixtures/snapshots/funding_inputs/treasury_auctions/20260914T051023Z_722359ea9bc7.json (Fiscal Data auctions_query, retrieved 2026-09-14T05:10:23Z) dates every auction's announcement by announcemt_date, with no clock time, and in all 3828 records the announcement is on or before the auction date and the settlement date. For auctions settling inside the panel the announcement is, in calendar days before settlement, one to eleven for bills (7 for 2184 of 2360) and three to twenty-one for notes and bonds. Treasury publishes no clock time for an individual announcement: the TreasuryDirect page 'How auctions work' (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/auctions/how-auctions-work/, read 11 October 2026) lists what each announcement carries (security, amount, auction date, issue date) and says only that the list of upcoming auctions is 'Updated every Friday by 10:45 AM, Eastern U.S. time'. The 12:00 instant therefore rests on the usual late-morning announcement time plus an hour, as metadata/net_settlement.json's 12:00 does (#426), and it was NOT verified against a published clock time from this environment. It is before the 16:00 decision every published run uses, so any instant from 11:00 to 15:59 gives the same sums at that decision; the setting is flagged for Eleonora in the pull request. repo_model.settlement_dating.auction_results refuses a record announced after its auction or its settlement.
